chunks: Al-Fadl from Ibn Mahbub from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf from some of the companions of Abu Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the daughters of a sister and a grandfather, he said: 'For the daughters of the sister is one-third, and whatever remains is for the grandfather. Thus, he established the daughters of the sister in the place of the sister, and made the grandfather in the position of the brother.'
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of the paternal grandfather when inheriting with the daughters of a sister?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the specific inheritance dynamics between the daughters of a sister (banat al-ukht) and the paternal grandfather (al-jadd), establishing a fractional share (thuluth) for the former and the residue for the latter. Shaykh al-Tusi highlights the juristic principle of *ta'sib* (residuary inheritance) by equating the grandfather's status to that of a brother in this context, a key point of discussion among Shia scholars regarding whether the grandfather is treated as a direct ancestor or a collateral relative. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia inheritance law in accommodating complex family structures by adjusting the shares of residual heirs based on the presence of specific descendants.
